1	# Telegram Near-Liquidation Alerts
2	
3	PANIK sends a Telegram message when a monitored wallet's position crosses into
4	the user's risk zone (a profile-relative status transition toward liquidation).
5	This doc covers setup, the moving parts, and the anti-spam design.
6	
7	## Moving parts
8	
9	| Piece | Where | Runtime | Notes |
10	|-------|-------|---------|-------|
11	| Trigger | `packages/scoring/src/profile.ts` (`statusFor`) | pure | within / approaching / outside vs the profile threshold (25 / 50 / 75) |
12	| Debounce | `packages/scoring/src/watch/loop.ts` (`WatchService.confirmTicks`) | worker | a status must hold N consecutive 60s ticks before it emits |
13	| Send gate | `packages/scoring/src/watch/alertPolicy.ts` (`decideSend`) | worker | materiality + cooldown + escalation bypass |
14	| Message copy | `packages/scoring/src/watch/alertMessage.ts` (`formatAlert`) | worker | plain text, hyphens only |
15	| Worker | `scripts/watch-worker.ts` (`npm run worker`) | standalone | scores, persists transitions, dispatches |
16	| Send | `server/telegram.ts` (`sendMessage`) | worker + webhook | Bot API, fetch-only |
17	| Link store | `server/telegramStore.ts` | Vercel functions | Supabase REST, no pg/viem |
18	| Mint code | `/api/telegram/link` | Railway api-server (`scripts/api-server.ts`) | `api/telegram/link.ts` is the Vercel fallback |
19	| Webhook | `/api/telegram/webhook` | Railway api-server | `api/telegram/webhook.ts` is the Vercel fallback; receives `/start <code>` and `/stop` |
20	| Register wallet | `register_watched_wallet` RPC | browser (publishable key) | called from onboarding |
21	| Schema | `supabase/migrations/20260627000001_telegram_alerts.sql` | Supabase | `telegram_links`, `telegram_link_codes`, the RPC |
22	
23	## Data flow
24	
25	1. The user onboards (wallet-connect is mandatory). On completion the browser
26	   calls `register_watched_wallet(wallet, profile)`, upserting a row into
27	   `public.watched_wallets`. The worker now scores that wallet.
28	2. In the Settings tab the user clicks **Connect Telegram**. The browser POSTs
29	   `/api/telegram/link`, which mints a single-use, 15-minute code in
30	   `telegram_link_codes` and returns `t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`. The browser
31	   opens it.
32	3. The user presses Start. Telegram POSTs the update to
33	   `/api/telegram/webhook` (with the secret header). The webhook resolves the
34	   code to the wallet, upserts `telegram_links(wallet, chat_id)`, deletes the
35	   code, and replies with a confirmation. `/stop` disables the link.
36	4. The worker scores every active wallet each 60s. On a confirmed profile-status
37	   transition it inserts a `watch_transitions` row (`notified_at` NULL). The
38	   dispatch loop (15s) joins unnotified rows to `telegram_links`, applies the
39	   send gate, sends, and stamps `notified_at` + `notify_channel`.
40	
41	## Anti-spam / false-alarm controls
42	
43	The backtest (`BACKTEST_METHODOLOGY.md`) documents a ~24-27% intrinsic
44	false-alarm rate, so notification volume is governed at the delivery layer.
45	Knobs live in `ALERT_POLICY` (`packages/scoring/src/params.ts`):
46	
47	- **confirmTicks (3)** - a candidate status must hold 3 consecutive 60s ticks
48	  before it emits. Kills single-tick spikes (flaky RPC, price wick) and
49	  threshold flapping. ~3 min vs the backtest's tens-of-hours lead times.
50	- **cooldownMs (6h)** - at most one alert per (wallet, protocol) per window. An
51	  escalation (approaching to outside) bypasses the cooldown.
52	- **minBorrowUsd ($50)** - positions with no debt (HF null) or sub-dust borrow
53	  never alert; they cannot be liquidated regardless of composite score.
54	
55	`notify_channel` records the outcome for every transition: `telegram` (sent),
56	`skipped` (recovery), `suppressed_cooldown`, `suppressed_immaterial`, `blocked`
57	(user blocked the bot). Honest scope: these cut nuisance volume and
58	safe-position noise, not the calibrated precision/recall point.
59	
60	## Setup
61	
62	1. Apply the migration in the Supabase SQL Editor (idempotent).
63	2. Create a bot via **@BotFather**; copy the token. Choose a random
64	   `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Set the bot username.
65	   ```
66	   TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123456:ABC...
67	   TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=<random>
68	   VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME=YourPanikBot
69	   TELEGRAM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-railway-web-domain
70	   ```
71	3. Register the webhook once per environment:
72	   ```
73	   npm run telegram:setup            # uses TELEGRAM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
74	   npm run telegram:setup -- <url>   # or pass a tunnel URL for local testing
75	   ```
76	4. Deploy the worker (host-agnostic via `Dockerfile` / `Procfile`):
77	   - **Fly.io** (cheapest always-on): a single shared-cpu-1x 256MB machine with
78	     `min_machines_running = 1`, ~cents/month.
79	   - **Railway** (easiest): deploy from repo, the `Procfile` runs `npm run worker`,
80	     ~$5/mo hobby.
81	   - Avoid Render's free tier (background workers sleep).
82	   Worker env: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_DB_URL`,
83	   `ALCHEMY_API_KEY_BASE_MAINNET`, `COINGECKO_API_KEY`.
84	   Vercel env: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`,
85	   `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME`, plus the existing `SUPABASE_URL` /
86	   `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`.
87	
88	## Local end-to-end test
89	
90	1. `npm run dev:api` and `npm run dev`. The dev api-server mirrors
91	   `/api/telegram/link`, so **Connect Telegram** works locally.
92	2. Expose the dev server (or `vercel dev`) via a tunnel (`cloudflared`/`ngrok`)
93	   and run `npm run telegram:setup -- <tunnel-url>` so the webhook is reachable.
94	3. The seed wallet `0x76f88702325c92c83efad341a932fb326957056f`
95	   ("validation: Moonwell HF~1.2 (alerts)") is a good low-HF target. To force a
96	   transition fast, temporarily set its `risk_profile='conservative'`.
97	4. `npm run worker:dev`. Watch the logs: it seeds prior statuses, scores the
98	   cohort, writes a `score_snapshots` row, and inserts a `watch_transitions` row.
99	5. Onboard with that wallet, click Connect Telegram, press Start, then watch the
100	   dispatcher send the alert and stamp `notified_at`. Send `/stop` to disable.
101	
```

1	/**
2	 * Telegram Bot API send helper. Pure fetch (no viem/pg), so it bundles cleanly
3	 * in a Vercel serverless function and also runs in the standalone worker.
4	 *
5	 * The dispatcher stamps watch_transitions.notified_at only when ok === true, so
6	 * a transient failure (429/5xx) leaves the row for the next poll.
7	 */
8	
9	export interface TelegramSendResult {
10	  /** Telegram's own ok flag (its JSON body), AND the HTTP request succeeded. */
11	  ok: boolean;
12	  /** HTTP status (or 0 if the request never completed). */
13	  status: number;
14	  /** Telegram error_code when ok is false (e.g. 403 = blocked, 429 = rate). */
15	  errorCode?: number;
16	  description?: string;
17	}
18	
19	export interface SendOptions {
20	  parseMode?: "MarkdownV2" | "HTML";
21	  disablePreview?: boolean;
22	  signal?: AbortSignal;
23	}
24	
25	/**
26	 * POST sendMessage. Returns a structured result instead of throwing so callers
27	 * can branch on errorCode (403 -> disable link, 429 -> back off, else retry).
28	 */
29	export async function sendMessage(
30	  token: string,
31	  chatId: number | string,
32	  text: string,
33	  opts: SendOptions = {},
34	): Promise<TelegramSendResult> {
35	  let res: Response;
36	  try {
37	    res = await fetch(`https://api.telegram.org/bot${token}/sendMessage`, {
38	      method: "POST",
39	      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
40	      body: JSON.stringify({
41	        chat_id: chatId,
42	        text,
43	        parse_mode: opts.parseMode,
44	        disable_web_page_preview: opts.disablePreview ?? true,
45	      }),
46	      signal: opts.signal,
47	    });
48	  } catch (err) {
49	    return { ok: false, status: 0, description: (err as Error).message };
50	  }
51	
52	  let body: { ok?: boolean; error_code?: number; description?: string } = {};
53	  try {
54	    body = (await res.json()) as typeof body;
55	  } catch {
56	    // Non-JSON body (rare); fall back to HTTP status.
57	  }
58	
59	  return {
60	    ok: res.ok && body.ok === true,
61	    status: res.status,
62	    errorCode: body.error_code,
63	    description: body.description,
64	  };
65	}
66	
67	/**
68	 * Register the bot's webhook with Telegram (idempotent). Called on API boot so
69	 * /start updates are delivered without a manual `telegram:setup`. `secret` is
70	 * echoed back by Telegram in the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header, which
71	 * the webhook handler checks.
72	 */
73	export async function setWebhook(
74	  token: string,
75	  url: string,
76	  secret: string,
77	): Promise<TelegramSendResult> {
78	  let res: Response;
79	  try {
80	    res = await fetch(`https://api.telegram.org/bot${token}/setWebhook`, {
81	      method: "POST",
82	      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
83	      body: JSON.stringify({ url, secret_token: secret, allowed_updates: ["message"] }),
84	    });
85	  } catch (err) {
86	    return { ok: false, status: 0, description: (err as Error).message };
87	  }
88	  let body: { ok?: boolean; error_code?: number; description?: string } = {};
89	  try {
90	    body = (await res.json()) as typeof body;
91	  } catch {
92	    // Non-JSON body (rare); fall back to HTTP status.
93	  }
94	  return { ok: res.ok && body.ok === true, status: res.status, errorCode: body.error_code, description: body.description };
95	}
96

12	  wallet: string;
13	  expiresAt: number; // epoch ms
14	}

16	export class TelegramStore {
17	  private readonly base: string;
18

20	    supabaseUrl: string,
21	    private readonly serviceKey: string,
22	  ) {
23	    this.base = supabaseUrl.replace(/\/+$/, "");
24	  }
25	
26	  /** Build from env; throws if unconfigured (caller maps to 503). */
27	  static fromEnv(): TelegramStore {
28	    const url = process.env.SUPABASE_URL;
29	    const key = process.env.SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY;
30	    if (!url || !key) throw new Error("SUPABASE_URL / SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY missing");

33

41	  }
42

46	  async createLinkCode(code: string, wallet: string, ttlMs: number): Promise<void> {
47	    const expires = new Date(Date.now() + ttlMs).toISOString();
48	    const res = await fetch(`${this.base}/rest/v1/telegram_link_codes`, {

58	    const url =

60	      `?code=eq.${encodeURIComponent(code)}&select=wallet,expires_at&limit=1`;

1	-- ============================================================================
2	-- PANIK - Telegram alerts schema v1 (2026-06-27)
3	-- Scope: deliver "near liquidation" alerts to Telegram for the onboarded user's
4	--        own wallet. Two new tables + one RPC. Idempotent (safe to re-run).
5	--
6	-- ADDITIVE ONLY. Touches none of the scoring objects except by referencing
7	-- public.watched_wallets via the register RPC. No changes to watch_transitions
8	-- (its notified_at / notify_channel columns are already the alert queue).
9	--
10	-- Access model (same as the rest of the project):
11	--   * Watch worker (direct pg) and Vercel webhook (Supabase REST + secret key)
12	--     bypass RLS. All new tables are deny-all RLS (zero policies).
13	--   * The browser registers its onboarded wallet through ONE SECURITY DEFINER
14	--     door: public.register_watched_wallet(), granted to anon (publishable key),
15	--     mirroring public.waitlist_signup(). No new secret reaches the frontend.
16	--
17	-- Link flow:
18	--   browser -> POST /api/telegram/link mints a row in telegram_link_codes and
19	--   returns t.me/<bot>?start=<code>. The user presses Start; the Telegram
20	--   webhook resolves the (single-use, TTL'd) code to a wallet and upserts
21	--   telegram_links(chat_id). The dispatcher joins watch_transitions.wallet =
22	--   telegram_links.wallet to find where to send.
23	-- ============================================================================
24	
25	create extension if not exists pgcrypto;
26	
27	-- ── 1. telegram_links - durable wallet -> chat join target ──────────────────
28	-- One wallet maps to one chat and vice-versa. A re-link (same chat, new wallet)
29	-- is handled in the webhook by deleting the prior chat_id row before upsert.
30	create table if not exists public.telegram_links (
31	  wallet     text primary key
32	             check (wallet = lower(wallet) and wallet ~ '^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$'),
33	  chat_id    bigint not null unique,
34	  username   text,
35	  enabled    boolean not null default true,
36	  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
37	  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
38	);
39	
40	drop trigger if exists trg_telegram_links_updated on public.telegram_links;
41	create trigger trg_telegram_links_updated
42	  before update on public.telegram_links
43	  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();
44	
45	-- ── 2. telegram_link_codes - ephemeral deep-link codes ──────────────────────
46	-- Single-use (deleted on consume), TTL-bounded (expiry checked in the webhook).
47	create table if not exists public.telegram_link_codes (
48	  code       text primary key,
49	  wallet     text not null
50	             check (wallet = lower(wallet) and wallet ~ '^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$'),
51	  expires_at timestamptz not null,
52	  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
53	);
54	
55	create index if not exists idx_telegram_link_codes_expires
56	  on public.telegram_link_codes (expires_at);
57	
58	-- ── 3. RLS - deny-all default (worker/webhook use secret key / direct pg) ────
59	alter table public.telegram_links      enable row level security;
60	alter table public.telegram_link_codes enable row level security;
61	-- No policies on purpose: publishable-key clients get nothing here. The only
62	-- browser-facing write is register_watched_wallet() below (SECURITY DEFINER).
63	
64	-- ── 4. register_watched_wallet - browser registers its onboarded wallet ─────
65	-- Mirrors public.waitlist_signup: deny-all table + ONE SECURITY DEFINER door
66	-- granted to anon. Idempotent on the wallet unique constraint; a re-onboard
67	-- refreshes risk_profile and re-activates the row. Silent no-op for non-EVM
68	-- (Solana) addresses, which the on-chain readers cannot monitor.
69	create or replace function public.register_watched_wallet(
70	  p_wallet  text,
71	  p_profile text
72	) returns void
73	language plpgsql
74	security definer
75	set search_path = public
76	as $$
77	declare
78	  v_wallet  text := lower(btrim(coalesce(p_wallet, '')));
79	  v_profile text := lower(btrim(coalesce(p_profile, '')));
80	begin
81	  if v_wallet !~ '^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$' then
82	    return; -- non-EVM or malformed: nothing to monitor
83	  end if;
84	  if v_profile not in ('conservative','moderate','aggressive') then
85	    v_profile := 'moderate';
86	  end if;
87	
88	  insert into public.watched_wallets (wallet, risk_profile, label)
89	  values (v_wallet, v_profile, 'onboarded user')
90	  on conflict (wallet) do update
91	    set risk_profile = excluded.risk_profile,
92	        is_active    = true,
93	        updated_at   = now();
94	end $$;
95	
96	grant execute on function public.register_watched_wallet(text, text) to anon, authenticated;
97	
98	-- ── 5. Retention - expire stale link codes (pg_cron) ────────────────────────
99	-- Separate job; does NOT touch the existing panik_retention schedule.
100	create extension if not exists pg_cron;
101	
102	do $$ begin perform cron.unschedule('panik_telegram_codes_cleanup'); exception when others then null; end $$;
103	select cron.schedule(
104	  'panik_telegram_codes_cleanup',
105	  '23 * * * *',  -- hourly at :23
106	  $$ delete from public.telegram_link_codes where expires_at < now() - interval '1 day'; $$
107	);
108	
```

### 🤖 Claude *(2026-07-03 08:30:38)*

I've traced the whole flow. Here's how it works.

## Short answer

Alerts are keyed on the **wallet address**, and delivered to Telegram via the **`chat_id`** (Telegram's internal numeric ID for the chat). The **`@username` is captured but purely cosmetic** - it's never used to route, monitor, or deliver anything.

## The chain

**1. Wallet is what's monitored.** On onboarding, the browser calls `register_watched_wallet(wallet, profile)`, which upserts the address into `watched_wallets`. The worker scores wallets, not people.

**2. Linking ties a wallet to a chat.** In Settings, "Connect Telegram" mints a single-use, 15-min code (`telegram_link_codes`) bound to the wallet, and opens `t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`. When the user presses Start, Telegram's webhook resolves the code back to the wallet and writes a row in [telegram_links](supabase/migrations/20260627000001_telegram_alerts.sql#L30-L38):

```
wallet   (PK)      -- the join key
chat_id  (unique)  -- where the message actually goes
username           -- captured for display only
```

**3. Delivery uses `chat_id`, not username.** The dispatcher joins `watch_transitions.wallet = telegram_links.wallet` to find the chat, then calls [sendMessage(token, chatId, text)](server/telegram.ts#L29-L47) - the Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` takes `chat_id`. Username never enters the send path.

## Why username is only cosmetic

- In [upsertLink](server/telegramStore.ts#L84-L101) the username is stored as an optional field (`username ?? null`) alongside the real routing keys.
- Per recent commits (`auto-confirm connect + show captured @username`), it's captured so the UI can show *"Connected as @foo"* as confirmation feedback - a human-readable label, nothing more.
- `chat_id` is the durable, unique identifier. Usernames can change or be absent entirely; `chat_id` is stable, which is why it's the `unique` constraint and the `/stop` disable key.

So: **monitoring = wallet address, delivery = chat_id, username = display label only.**

One nuance worth flagging: because the link is 1:1 on both `wallet` and `chat_id`, one Telegram chat can only be linked to one wallet at a time (re-linking deletes the prior `chat_id` row). If you ever want a single user to get alerts for multiple wallets, that's a schema change, not a config tweak.

209	  profileFor: (wallet) => profileByWallet.get(wallet.toLowerCase()) ?? "moderate",
210	  onTransition: (t) => void persistTransition(t),
211	  onError: (err, wallet) =>
212	    console.error(`score failed for ${wallet}: ${(err as Error).message.slice(0, 100)}`),
213	  intervalMs: TICK_MS,
214	  confirmTicks: ALERT_POLICY.confirmTicks,
215	});
216	
217	/** Seed last committed status from the persisted transition tail (restart dedupe). */
218	async function seedLastStatus(): Promise<void> {
219	  const { rows } = await db.query<{ wallet: string; protocol: Protocol; to_status: ProfileStatus }>(
220	    `select distinct on (wallet, protocol) wallet, protocol, to_status
221	       from public.watch_transitions
222	      order by wallet, protocol, created_at desc`,
223	  );
224	  for (const r of rows) service.seed(r.wallet, r.protocol, r.to_status);
225	  console.log(`seeded ${rows.length} prior statuses`);
226	}
227	
228	// ── dispatch loop ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
229	interface PendingRow {
230	  id: string;
231	  wallet: string;
232	  protocol: Protocol;
233	  risk_profile: RiskProfile;
234	  score: number;
235	  band: WatchTransition["band"];
236	  to_status: ProfileStatus;
237	  created_at: string;
238	  chat_id: string;
239	  health_factor: string | null;
240	  collateral_usd: string | null;
241	  borrow_usd: string | null;
242	}
243	
244	async function stamp(id: string, channel: string): Promise<void> {
245	  await db.query(
246	    "update public.watch_transitions set notified_at = now(), notify_channel = $2 where id = $1",
247	    [id, channel],
248	  );
249	}
250	
251	async function dispatchPending(): Promise<void> {
252	  // First, mark recovery transitions (to_status = within) as seen so the queue
253	  // never accumulates them. They never notify.
254	  await db.query(
255	    "update public.watch_transitions set notified_at = now(), notify_channel = 'skipped' where notified_at is null and to_status = 'within'",
256	  );
257	
258	  const { rows } = await db.query<PendingRow>(
259	    `select t.id, t.wallet, t.protocol, t.risk_profile, t.score, t.band, t.to_status,
260	            t.created_at, l.chat_id,
261	            s.health_factor, s.collateral_usd, s.borrow_usd
262	       from public.watch_transitions t
263	       join public.telegram_links l on l.wallet = t.wallet and l.enabled
264	       left join lateral (
265	         select health_factor, collateral_usd, borrow_usd
266	           from public.score_snapshots s
267	          where s.wallet = t.wallet and s.protocol = t.protocol
268	          order by created_at desc limit 1
269	       ) s on true
270	      where t.notified_at is null and t.to_status in ('approaching','outside')
271	      order by t.created_at
272	      limit 50`,
273	  );
274	
275	  for (const r of rows) {
276	    const prior = await db.query<{ to_status: ProfileStatus; created_at: string }>(
277	      `select to_status, created_at from public.watch_transitions
278	        where wallet = $1 and protocol = $2 and notify_channel = 'telegram'
279	        order by created_at desc limit 1`,
280	      [r.wallet, r.protocol],
281	    );
282	    const priorRow = prior.rows[0];
283	
284	    const decision = decideSend({
285	      toStatus: r.to_status,
286	      createdAt: new Date(r.created_at).getTime(),
287	      healthFactor: r.health_factor == null ? null : Number(r.health_factor),
288	      borrowUsd: r.borrow_usd == null ? null : Number(r.borrow_usd),
289	      prior: priorRow
290	        ? { toStatus: priorRow.to_status, createdAt: new Date(priorRow.created_at).getTime() }
291	        : null,
292	    });
293	
294	    if (decision !== "send") {
295	      await stamp(r.id, decision);
296	      continue;
297	    }
298	
299	    const text = formatAlert(
300	      {
301	        wallet: r.wallet,
302	        protocol: r.protocol,
303	        profile: r.risk_profile,
304	        score: r.score,
305	        band: r.band,
306	        from: priorRow?.to_status ?? null,
307	        to: r.to_status,
308	      },
309	      {
310	        healthFactor: r.health_factor == null ? null : Number(r.health_factor),
311	        collateralUsd: r.collateral_usd == null ? null : Number(r.collateral_usd),
312	        borrowUsd: r.borrow_usd == null ? null : Number(r.borrow_usd),
313	      },
314	    );
315	
316	    const result = await sendMessage(botToken!, Number(r.chat_id), text);
317	    if (result.ok) {
318	      await stamp(r.id, "telegram");
319	    } else if (result.errorCode === 403) {
320	      // User blocked the bot / deleted the chat: terminal. Disable + stop retrying.
321	      await db.query("update public.telegram_links set enabled = false, updated_at = now() where chat_id = $1", [r.chat_id]);
322	      await stamp(r.id, "blocked");
323	      console.error(`telegram 403 for chat ${r.chat_id}; link disabled`);
324	    } else {
325	      // Transient (429/5xx/network): leave notified_at null for the next poll.
326	      console.error(`telegram send failed (status ${result.status}): ${result.description ?? ""}`.slice(0, 160));
327	    }
328	  }
329	}
330	
331	// ── boot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
332	let tickCount = 0;
333	
334	async function main(): Promise<void> {
335	  process.on("unhandledRejection", (reason) =>
336	    console.error(`unhandledRejection (kept alive): ${reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : String(reason)}`),
337	  );
338	
339	  await seedLastStatus();
340	  syncWatched(service, await loadWatched());
341	  console.log(`watching ${profileByWallet.size} wallets; confirmTicks=${ALERT_POLICY.confirmTicks}, cooldown=${ALERT_POLICY.cooldownMs / 3_600_000}h`);
342	
343	  // Drive ticks ourselves (instead of service.start()) so we can interleave the
344	  // periodic wallet reload on the same cadence.
345	  const runTick = async () => {
346	    tickCount += 1;
347	    if (tickCount % WALLET_RELOAD_EVERY_TICKS === 0) {
348	      try {
349	        syncWatched(service, await loadWatched());
350	      } catch (err) {
351	        console.error(`wallet reload skipped: ${(err as Error).message.slice(0, 100)}`);
352	      }
353	    }
354	    await service.tick();
355	  };
356	
357	  await runTick(); // warm immediately
358	  setInterval(() => void runTick(), TICK_MS);
359	  setInterval(() => void dispatchPending().catch((e) => console.error(`dispatch error: ${(e as Error).message.slice(0, 120)}`)), DISPATCH_MS);
360	
361	  console.log("watch worker running");
362	}
363	
364	void main().catch((err) => {
365	  console.error(`worker fatal: ${(err as Error).message}`);
366	  process.exit(1);
367	});
368

1	/**
2	 * Dispatcher send-decision: the anti-spam / false-alarm gate applied to a
3	 * confirmed transition BEFORE a Telegram message goes out. Pure given inputs so
4	 * it is unit-testable; the worker (scripts/watch-worker.ts) supplies the rows.
5	 *
6	 * Layers (see params.ALERT_POLICY and the plan's anti-spam section):
7	 *  1. Materiality: no debt (HF null) or sub-dust borrow never alerts - a "safe"
8	 *     position cannot be liquidated, whatever its composite score.
9	 *  2. Escalation bypass: approaching -> outside always sends (strictly worse).
10	 *  3. Cooldown: otherwise at most one alert per (wallet, protocol) per window.
11	 *
12	 * Recovery transitions (to_status === "within") are filtered out upstream and
13	 * never reach this function.
14	 */
15	
16	import { ALERT_POLICY } from "../params";
17	import type { ProfileStatus } from "../types";
18	
19	/** The most recent Telegram alert actually SENT for this (wallet, protocol). */
20	export interface PriorAlert {
21	  toStatus: ProfileStatus;
22	  /** epoch ms */
23	  createdAt: number;
24	}
25	
26	export interface SendDecisionInput {
27	  /** "approaching" | "outside" (recovery filtered earlier). */
28	  toStatus: ProfileStatus;
29	  /** This transition's timestamp (epoch ms). */
30	  createdAt: number;
31	  /** Latest known health factor; null = no debt. */
32	  healthFactor: number | null;
33	  /** Latest known borrow value in USD; null/0 = no debt. */
34	  borrowUsd: number | null;
35	  /** Last sent alert for this position, or null if none. */
36	  prior: PriorAlert | null;
37	}
38	
39	export type SendReason = "send" | "suppressed_immaterial" | "suppressed_cooldown";
40	
41	export function decideSend(input: SendDecisionInput): SendReason {
42	  // 1. Materiality: a position with no real debt cannot be liquidated.
43	  if (input.healthFactor == null || !Number.isFinite(input.healthFactor)) {
44	    return "suppressed_immaterial";
45	  }
46	  if (input.borrowUsd == null || input.borrowUsd < ALERT_POLICY.minBorrowUsd) {
47	    return "suppressed_immaterial";
48	  }
49	
50	  const prior = input.prior;
51	  if (!prior) return "send"; // first alert for this position
52	
53	  // 2. Escalation: approaching -> outside is worse news; bypass the cooldown.
54	  if (input.toStatus === "outside" && prior.toStatus === "approaching") return "send";
55	
56	  // 3. Cooldown ceiling.
57	  if (input.createdAt - prior.createdAt >= ALERT_POLICY.cooldownMs) return "send";
58	
59	  return "suppressed_cooldown";
60	}
61	
```

Prints the row id\n * (for cleanup) and then polls until notified_at is stamped.\n */\nimport pg from \"pg\";\n\nconst WALLET = \"0x894a133b6e91fe68e06e4fdffcf5d267e4499eec\";\n\nconst db = new pg.Pool({\n  connectionString: process.env.SUPABASE_DB_URL,\n  ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false },\n});\n\nasync function main() {\n  const ins = await db.query<{ id: string; created_at: string }>(\n    `insert into public.watch_transitions\n       (wallet, protocol, risk_profile, score, band, from_status, to_status)\n     values ($1, 'morpho', 'moderate', 62, 'HIGH', 'within', 'outside')\n     returning id, created_at`,\n    [WALLET],\n  );\n  const id = ins.rows[0].id;\n  console.log(`inserted watch_transitions id=${id} at ${ins.rows[0].created_at}`);\n\n  // Poll for the dispatcher (15s cadence) to stamp the row.\n  for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {\n    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000));\n    const { rows } = await db.query(\n      \"select notified_at, notify_channel from public.watch_transitions where id = $1\",\n      [id],\n    );\n    const row = rows[0];\n    process.stdout.write(`poll ${i + 1}: notify_channel=${row.notify_channel ?? \"null\"}\\n`);\n    if (row.notified_at) {\n      console.log(`RESULT: notified_at=${row.notified_at} channel=${row.notify_channel}`);\n      await db.end();\n      return;\n    }\n  }\n  console.log(\"TIMEOUT: row not stamped after 60s (is the worker running?)\");\n  await db.end();\n  process.exit(2);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });\n"

### 🤖 Claude *(2026-07-03 08:58:18)*

Done. The alert was delivered to the wallet's connected Telegram.

## What was sent

To **@nemoweb3** (chat_id `6662687823`), the chat linked to `0x894a...9eec`:

> **Panik alert - position past your risk limit**
>
> Wallet 0x894a...9eec
> Protocol Morpho
> Risk score 62 / 100 (HIGH), your moderate limit is 50
> Health factor 1.86
> Position $2,089 collateral / $675 debt
>
> Your position has crossed your risk threshold and is trending toward liquidation. Act now: add collateral or repay debt to pull it back.

(Position facts - HF 1.86, $2,089 / $675 - are the wallet's **real** live Morpho snapshot; the score 62 / "outside" status was injected for the test, since the real score is 28 / ELEVATED, safely within limits.)

## How it ran - through the real pipeline, not a shortcut

1. **Preflight**: wallet is linked (`telegram_links` enabled), watched (moderate profile), has a material position ($675 borrow ≥ $50 gate), no prior alert (no cooldown).
2. **Injection**: inserted a `watch_transitions` row (`to_status='outside'`, `notified_at` NULL) - exactly what the worker writes on a confirmed status change.
3. **Dispatch**: the deployed Railway worker's 15s loop picked it up, joined the link on the wallet address, passed `decideSend`, called the Bot API with the **chat_id**, and stamped the row - `notify_channel='telegram'` confirmed **4 seconds** after insert.
4. **Cleanup**: deleted the test row (so it can't suppress a real alert via the 6h cooldown) and removed the temp scripts. Working tree is back to how it was.

Note: no `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` exists locally - only the deployed worker holds it - which is why injecting into the queue was the correct (and more faithful) test: it proved the production worker, link join, send gate, and delivery stamping all work end to end.

### 🤖 Claude *(2026-07-03 09:34:31)*

Done. Onboarding now accepts **Base (EVM `0x...`) addresses only** - Solana addresses are rejected at the door.

## What changed

**[Onboarding.tsx](src/panik-core/components/Onboarding.tsx)** (the only code change):
- [isPlausibleWalletAddress](src/panik-core/components/Onboarding.tsx#L24-L28) - dropped the base58/Solana branch; EVM regex only. Doc comment now explains *why*: the analyzer, alert worker, and every backend table are EVM-only, so a Solana address onboards into a dead end (never monitored, never alerted).
- Error copy → `"That doesn't look like a valid Base (0x...) address."`
- Placeholder → `"0x... your Base wallet address"`

**[QA_TEST_GUIDE.md](docs/QA_TEST_GUIDE.md)** - B1 expectations updated to the new copy, plus a new check that base58 addresses must be rejected; B3's "Solana address" note removed.

## What I deliberately left alone

- **Backend/migrations** - nothing to change: `waitlist_signups`, `watched_wallets`, `wallet_profiles`, and `telegram_links` already enforce `^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$` via check constraints, and `register_watched_wallet` already no-ops on non-EVM input. That guard stays as defense-in-depth. No Solana address exists (or could exist) in the DB.
- **`cspell.json`** - keeps the "solana" word since the applied migration's comment still mentions it.

## Verified

- Validator unit-tested: 6/6 cases pass (valid Base lower/checksum-case + whitespace-trimmed → accept; Solana base58, `0x123`, empty → reject).
- `tsc --noEmit`: the only 3 errors are pre-existing wagmi typing issues in `panik-founding` - confirmed identical on clean HEAD via stash/re-run.

Diff is 1 file, +7/-9 (plus the untracked QA guide). Not committed - say the word if you want it committed.

### 🤖 Claude *(2026-07-03 09:42:54)*

Done - all three Telegram messages now lead with severity/context emojis. Full suite passes: **136 tests / 15 files**, including 4 new emoji assertions.

## The new formats

**🚨 Outside (worst case)** - as it would render for the QA wallet:

> 🚨 Panik alert - position past your risk limit
>
> 👛 Wallet 0x894a...9eec
> 🏦 Protocol Morpho
> 📊 Risk score 62 / 100 (HIGH), your moderate limit is 50
> 💔 Health factor 1.08 - near liquidation
> 💰 Position $2,089 collateral / $675 debt
>
> ⛔ Your position has crossed your risk threshold and is trending toward liquidation. Act now: add collateral or repay debt to pull it back.

**⚠️ Approaching** - same fact lines, softer framing, and the heart stays whole (❤️ at HF 1.86 vs 💔 below 1.15).

**👋 Welcome** - 🔗 linked wallet, 🛡️ promise line, 🔕 /stop, closes with 🧡 (brand orange).

## Design choices

- **Header emoji = severity signal**: 🚨 vs ⚠️ is the first character in the Telegram push-notification preview, so users can triage from the lock screen without opening the chat.
- **Stable pictograms per fact line** (👛 🏦 📊 💰): the eye can jump to a field without reading labels.
- **💔/❤️ health-factor flip** below the near-liquidation threshold (1.15) - the one line whose emoji carries state, tested both ways.
- **All existing copy preserved verbatim** - emojis are prefixes only, so every prior test assertion (wording, house-style no-long-dash checks, HF omission when null) still passes untouched. Plain text needs no MarkdownV2 escaping, emojis included.

## Files touched

- [alertMessage.ts](packages/scoring/src/watch/alertMessage.ts) - formats + doc comment explaining the emoji scheme
- [alertMessage.test.ts](packages/scoring/tests/alertMessage.test.ts) - 3 new tests (severity header ×2 variants, pictogram/heart-flip, welcome emojis)
- [TELEGRAM_ALERTS.md](docs/technical-docs/TELEGRAM_ALERTS.md#L14) - table row updated

One operational note: the **deployed Railway worker still sends the old format** until this is deployed - the message is built worker-side at send time. Once you're happy with the copy, this ships with the next deploy (and I can re-run the live wallet test afterward to confirm the emoji version lands in Telegram). Not committed yet - want me to?

  "content": "/**\n * Inject a test transition for the QA wallet so the newly deployed dispatcher\n * sends the emoji-format alert through the production pipeline. Prints the row\n * id, polls until notified_at is stamped, then deletes the test row so it\n * cannot trip the 6h cooldown for real alerts.\n */\nimport pg from \"pg\";\n\nconst WALLET = \"0x894a133b6e91fe68e06e4fdffcf5d267e4499eec\";\n\nconst db = new pg.Pool({\n  connectionString: process.env.SUPABASE_DB_URL,\n  ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false },\n});\n\nasync function main() {\n  const ins = await db.query<{ id: string }>(\n    `insert into public.watch_transitions\n       (wallet, protocol, risk_profile, score, band, from_status, to_status)\n     values ($1, 'morpho', 'moderate', 62, 'HIGH', 'within', 'outside')\n     returning id`,\n    [WALLET],\n  );\n  const id = ins.rows[0].id;\n  console.log(`inserted watch_transitions id=${id}`);\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {\n    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000));\n    const { rows } = await db.query(\n      \"select notified_at, notify_channel from public.watch_transitions where id = $1\",\n      [id],\n    );\n    if (rows[0].notified_at) {\n      console.log(`RESULT: channel=${rows[0].notify_channel} at ${rows[0].notified_at}`);\n      const del = await db.query(\"delete from public.watch_transitions where id = $1\", [id]);\n      console.log(`cleanup: deleted ${del.rowCount} test row`);\n      await db.end();\n      return;\n    }\n  }\n  console.log(`TIMEOUT: row ${id} not stamped after 60s; leaving it for inspection`);\n  await db.end();\n  process.exit(2);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });\n"
}

### 🤖 Claude *(2026-07-03 11:12:32)*

Good reference - YO's UI is doing a few very specific things well, and they map cleanly onto the QA backlog. Here's what's worth stealing and where it lands in PANIK:

## What YO gets right (and how it translates)

**1. One hero number + a sparkline behind it (vault cards)**
Every card leads with a single big number (yield %) and a 30d trend chart *as the card background*, with a compact TVL / Risk / Chains footer. No stat-grid.

→ This is exactly the fix for **img3 (#5)**. The Compass card's `PROTOCOL INDEX 18 / POOL COUNT 12 / POSITION COUNT 9` row is three numbers nobody can act on. Replace with a 30d APY sparkline (data: DefiLlama's pool history API - we already run a `DefiLlamaProvider` for systemic risk, so the integration point exists) and a one-line footer: `APY 5.2% · TVL $8.4m`. The hero number on a PANIK card stays the **risk score** - that's our product - with yield as the trend line, which is also an honest visual: "here's the yield you're chasing, here's the risk grade on it."

**2. Preset chips before free-form input (Time machine)**
Deposit is `$50K / $100K / $250K / $1M` chips, timeframe is `7D / 30D` chips. Custom entry exists but presets carry the interaction.

→ This is Elfritz's scenario suggestion for **img1 (#3)**, solved. The sandbox leads with sliders (expensive to think about); it should lead with scenario chips:

```
[ CURRENT ]  [ STRESS -20% ]  [ CRASH -40% ]  [ BLACK SWAN -55% ]
              HF 1.42          HF 1.08          HF 0.83
              safe             near liq ⚠️      LIQUIDATED 🚨
```

One tap = full answer. Sliders and the amount/price inputs Elfritz asked for (**#4**) move into an "Advanced" section below. Bonus rigor: the black-swan magnitude shouldn't be arbitrary - pull it from the backtest event set in `BACKTEST_METHODOLOGY.md`, and label it ("ETH, May 2021: -55% in 7 days"). That's a credibility detail YO can't match.

**3. Concrete-dollar framing over percentages**
"+$391.97 ahead of just holding ETH" and "every week you wait, you're leaving ~$91.46 on the table." Not "0.16% outperformance."

→ Apply to the simulator verdict: instead of only `HF 0.95`, say **"a -18% WETH move liquidates ~$1,940 of your collateral"**. Loss-framing is *more* natural for a risk product than for a yield product - this is arguably a bigger win for us than for YO.

**4. Risk as a single word on the card** (`Low` / `Moderate`)
We already have this (ELEVATED badge) - keep it, it's consistent with their pattern.

**5. Real-time deposits feed** - social proof ticker. Skip for now: alerts/positions are privacy-sensitive, and it doesn't answer any QA item.

## Updated backlog with the YO patterns folded in

| # | Item | Design decision |
|---|------|----------------|
| 2 | Score mismatch (42 vs 42/34/28) | Unchanged - investigate first, this is trust-critical |
| 3+4 | Simulator redesign | Scenario chips (Current/Stress/Crash/Black-swan from backtest events) + dollar-framed verdict; amount, borrow, and price inputs under Advanced |
| 5 | img3 stat row | 30d APY sparkline + `APY · TVL` footer via DefiLlama pool history |
| 6 | Risk breakdown panel | Add `8. APY` and `9. TVL (30d trend)` rows to the LIQUIDATION & POOL METRICS list - same DefiLlama call as #5, one data source feeds both |
| 1 | Favicon | Five-minute fix, unchanged |

One caution against over-copying YO: their entire UI exists to get money *in* (every element funnels to START EARNING). PANIK's job is judgment, not conversion - so borrow the information design (sparklines, chips, dollar framing), not the funnel energy (glow buttons everywhere, "leaving money on the table" urgency copy pointed at deposits).

Want me to start executing? Order I'd go: **#1 favicon → #2 score-mismatch investigation → #5+#6 (shared DefiLlama data layer) → #3+#4 simulator redesign**.

9	 * Calculates a DeFi position health factor and PANIK risk score.
10	 * Formula models general lending logic:
11	 * Max LTV is assumed to be 80% (0.80).
12	 * Health Factor = (Collateral * Max LTV) / Borrow
13	 */
14	export function calculateDynamicPosition(
15	  protocol: "Aave V3" | "Moonwell",
16	  collateral: number,
17	  borrow: number,
18	  collateralPrice: number
19	): PositionState {
20	  const maxLTV = protocol === "Aave V3" ? 0.82 : 0.78; // Aave is slightly higher blue-chip parameter
21	  const collateralValueUsd = (collateral * collateralPrice);
22	  const borrowValueUsd = borrow;
23	  
24	  // Calculate LTV
25	  const currentLTV = collateralValueUsd > 0 ? (borrowValueUsd / collateralValueUsd) : 0;
26	  
27	  // Calculate health factor
28	  // Health Factor = (Collateral Value * Max LTV) / Borrow Value
29	  let healthFactor = 100; // default if no borrow
30	  if (borrowValueUsd > 0) {
31	    healthFactor = (collateralValueUsd * maxLTV) / borrowValueUsd;
32	    // Cap or floor health factor for sanity
33	    healthFactor = Math.max(0.1, Math.min(9.99, healthFactor));
34	  }
35	
36	  // Calculate PANIK Risk Score (0 - 100)
37	  // Higher risk score means worse health.
38	  // When health factor is 1.0, risk score should be near 80.
39	  // When health factor reaches 2.5+, risk score is low (e.g. 15).
40	  // When health factor is near 1.1, risk score is highly critical (above 75).
41	  let riskScore = 0;
42	  if (healthFactor <= 1.0) {
43	    riskScore = Math.round(85 + (1.0 - healthFactor) * 15);
44	  } else if (healthFactor < 1.5) {
45	    // 1.0 to 1.5 is High Risk
46	    riskScore = Math.round(50 + ((1.5 - healthFactor) / 0.5) * 35);
47	  } else if (healthFactor < 2.5) {
48	    // 1.5 to 2.5 is Elevated
49	    riskScore = Math.round(25 + ((2.5 - healthFactor) / 1.0) * 25);
50	  } else {
51	    // 2.5 to 10 is Low
52	    riskScore = Math.round(Math.max(5, 25 - ((healthFactor - 2.5) / 7.5) * 20));
53	  }
54	
55	  riskScore = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, riskScore));
56	
57	  // Determine status category
58	  let status: "LOW" | "ELEVATED" | "HIGH" | "CRITICAL" = "LOW";
59	  if (riskScore >= 75) {
60	    status = "CRITICAL";
61	  } else if (riskScore >= 50) {
62	    status = "HIGH";
63	  } else if (riskScore >= 25) {
64	    status = "ELEVATED";
65	  }
66	
67	  // Dynamically calculate dynamic liquidation price of ETH
68	  // Borrow Value = Collateral ETH * LiquidationPrice * Max LTV
69	  // Liquidation Price = Borrow Value / (Collateral ETH * Max LTV)
70	  const collateralQty = collateral;
71	  const liquidationPrice = collateralQty > 0 
72	    ? Math.round(borrowValueUsd / (collateralQty * maxLTV)) 
73	    : 0;
74	
75	  // Generate recommendation plain language string
76	  let recommendation = "Position optimal. Collateral buffer protects against severe asset volatility.";
77	  if (status === "CRITICAL") {
78	    const repayAmount = Math.round(borrowValueUsd - (collateralValueUsd * maxLTV * 0.6));
79	    recommendation = `CRITICAL ALERT: Repay $${repayAmount} USDC immediately to prevent liquidator bids!`;
80	  } else if (status === "HIGH") {
81	    const repayAmount = Math.round(borrowValueUsd - (collateralValueUsd * maxLTV * 0.75));
82	    recommendation = `ACTION REQUIRED: Repay $${Math.max(50, repayAmount)} USDC to return health factor to a secure 1.75.`;
83	  } else if (status === "ELEVATED") {
84	    recommendation = `RECOMMENDED: Supply $${Math.round(collateralValueUsd * 0.15)} more collateral to suppress minor market swings.`;
85	  }
86	
87	  // Breakdowns
88	  const baseSafety = protocol === "Aave V3" ? 12 : 35; // Aave is highly audited, Moonwell has brief local history
89	  const systemic = status === "CRITICAL" ? 88 : status === "HIGH" ? 72 : status === "ELEVATED" ? 48 : 22;
90	
91	  return {
92	    protocol,
93	    assetPair: protocol === "Aave V3" ? "wstETH / USDC SUPPLY & BORROW" : "ETH / USDC BORROW",
94	    riskScore,
95	    status,
96	    collateralValue: collateralValueUsd,
97	    borrowValue: borrowValueUsd,
98	    healthFactor,
99	    liquidationPrice,
100	    currentPrice: collateralPrice,
101	    recommendation,
102	    breakdown: {
103	      positionHealth: Math.min(100, Math.round(currentLTV * 100)),
104	      assetVolatility: protocol === "Aave V3" ? 28 : 42, // Ether has moderate volatility, wstETH is derivative pegged
105	      protocolSafety: baseSafety,
106	      systemicMarketStress: systemic
107	    }
108	  };
109	}

{

  "content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport React, { useId } from \"react\";\n\n/**\n * Dependency-free inline sparkline: an SVG polyline with a soft area fill,\n * stretched to its container width. Used for the 30d APY trend on Compass\n * cards and in the risk-breakdown panel.\n */\nexport function Sparkline(props: {\n  data: number[];\n  /** CSS color for the line + gradient fill. */\n  stroke?: string;\n  /** Rendered height in px (width fills the container). */\n  height?: number;\n  className?: string;\n}) {\n  const { data, stroke = \"#34d399\", height = 36, className } = props;\n  const gradientId = useId();\n  if (data.length < 2) return null;\n\n  const W = 100;\n  const H = 32;\n  const PAD = 2;\n  const min = Math.min(...data);\n  const max = Math.max(...data);\n  const span = max - min || 1; // flat series still renders a midline\n  const points = data.map((v, i) => {\n    const x = (i / (data.length - 1)) * W;\n    const y = PAD + (1 - (v - min) / span) * (H - 2 * PAD);\n    return `${x.toFixed(2)},${y.toFixed(2)}`;\n  });\n  const line = points.join(\" \");\n  const area = `${line} ${W},${H} 0,${H}`;\n\n  return (\n    <svg\n      viewBox={`0 0 ${W} ${H}`}\n      preserveAspectRatio=\"none\"\n      width=\"100%\"\n      style={{ height }}\n      className={className}\n      aria-hidden=\"true\"\n    >\n      <defs>\n        <linearGradient id={gradientId} x1=\"0\" y1=\"0\" x2=\"0\" y2=\"1\">\n          <stop offset=\"0%\" stopColor={stroke} stopOpacity=\"0.22\" />\n          <stop offset=\"100%\" stopColor={stroke} stopOpacity=\"0\" />\n        </linearGradient>\n      </defs>\n      <polygon points={area} fill={`url(#${gradientId})`} />\n      <polyline\n        points={line}\n        fill=\"none\"\n        stroke={stroke}\n        strokeWidth=\"1.5\"\n        strokeLinejoin=\"round\"\n        vectorEffect=\"non-scaling-stroke\"\n      />\n    </svg>\n  );\n}\n"
}

Display-only;\n * keep in sync if the engine weights change.\n */\nconst SUB_SCORE_WEIGHTS = { positionHealth: 0.4, assetRisk: 0.25, protocolSafety: 0.2, systemicRisk: 0.15 } as const;\n\n/**\n * Offline-only sub-score estimates whose WEIGHTED SUM reproduces the composite\n * (the old UI showed fabricated Position/Pool/Protocol numbers that did not\n * reconcile with the headline score - the exact QA complaint). Live engine\n * sub-scores replace these whenever /api/compass is reachable.\n */\nfunction demoSubScores(total: number) {\n  const clamp = (n: number) => Math.max(0, Math.min(100, Math.round(n)));\n  const positionHealth = clamp(total + 12);\n  const assetRisk = clamp(total + 2);\n  const protocolSafety = clamp(total - 10);\n  const systemicRisk = clamp(\n    (total -\n      SUB_SCORE_WEIGHTS.positionHealth * positionHealth -\n      SUB_SCORE_WEIGHTS.assetRisk * assetRisk -\n      SUB_SCORE_WEIGHTS.protocolSafety * protocolSafety) /\n      SUB_SCORE_WEIGHTS.systemicRisk,\n  );\n  return { positionHealth, assetRisk, protocolSafety, systemicRisk };\n}\n\n/**\n * Simulator scenario presets (one-tap answers before sliders). All six QA items are done and visually verified against the live engine. Here's the full report:

## What shipped (working tree, not yet committed)

**1. Favicon** - generated a dark-tile set from the white logo (invisible on light tabs otherwise): `favicon.svg`, `favicon-32.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, linked in all three entry points ([index.html](index.html), [app.html](app.html), [founding.html](founding.html)). Bonus: `founding.html` pointed at `/panik-logo.svg` which **didn't exist** - fixed.

**2. Score mismatch (the trust-critical one)** - root cause: the breakdown panel **fabricated** its sub-scores (`Pool = baseRisk - 8`, `Protocol = baseRisk - 14`) so they could never reconcile with the headline. Now the panel renders the engine's real four components with their weights - and they check out on screen: **0.4·64 + 0.25·58 + 0.2·10 + 0.15·0 = 42**, exactly the headline. Health factor, liquidation price, and buffer now come from the live engine too, with a ● LIVE / DEMO chip so nobody mistakes fallback data for real (offline fallback estimates are now weighted-consistent instead of arbitrary).

**3+4. Simulator** - new **Price Scenarios** panel: Current / Stress -20% / Crash -40% (FTX week, Nov 2022) / Black swan -55% (ETH, Jun 2022) - magnitudes cited from the backtest event set, each chip showing implied price + HF preview, LIQUIDATED flagged in red. Plus the dollar-framed verdict Elfritz-style: *"At this simulated price your $3,600 collateral is past the liquidation threshold."* Advanced inputs added: collateral amount (new), collateral price, borrowed amount, and **borrowed-asset price** with a USDC-depeg slider (floor $0.85, annotated with the real Mar 2023 event). Price slider now reaches -60%.

**5+6. APY/TVL everywhere** - new `/api/poolhistory` endpoint (DefiLlama, 7 verified Base pool UUIDs, 1h cache, stale-cache fallback). Compass cards: fake Protocol/Pool/Position counts **deleted**, replaced with a 30d supply-APY sparkline + live APY + TVL. Breakdown panel: dimensions 8 (Supply APY + sparkline) and 9 (Pool TVL + sparkline) added, signals renumbered 10-12. Notable honesty win: real wstETH supply APY is **0.0%**, not the fabricated 5.2%.

## Verification

- **136/136 tests**, `vite build` clean, tsc shows only the 3 pre-existing `panik-founding` errors (confirmed identical on HEAD earlier)
- **Endpoint live-tested**: 7 pools, 30-point series each
- **Visually verified** in headless Edge against the real dev API - Compass sparklines, the reconciling breakdown panel, and the black-swan scenario driving the live engine to 75/CRITICAL all captured in screenshots

New files: `Sparkline.tsx` (dependency-free SVG), 3 favicon assets. Modified: `AppDemo.tsx`, `live.ts`, `utils.ts`, `api-server.ts`, 3 HTML entries.

Two notes for the team: the deployed Railway `risk-scoring` service picks up `/api/poolhistory` on next deploy (and remember the watch-worker doesn't auto-deploy); and Moonwell's cbETH market is no longer listed on DefiLlama, so that one card falls back to static APY with "history unavailable" - honest, not a bug.

Say the word and I'll commit + push (and can re-verify on production after Railway deploys).

### 🤖 Claude *(2026-07-03 13:39:54)*

All done - **6/6 E2E checks pass**, verified twice. The dev server on **http://localhost:3001/app** already has everything live (Vite hot-reloaded).

## What was fixed

**1. The misaligned wallet (the screenshot bug)** - root cause found: the right header chip renders `selectedWallet`, which got initialized from the *validation registry* before onboarding completed and was never re-synced afterward - so it kept showing a registry wallet (`0x12a5…2305`) forever. The sync effect now forces `selectedWallet` to track the onboarded wallet in bound mode ([AppDemo.tsx](src/panik-core/AppDemo.tsx)). Also removed the hardcoded `0x8F94…42fA` fallback.

**2. Change wallet** - the right header chip is now a button (hover shows a refresh icon + tooltip). Clicking it reopens onboarding:
- **New wallet** → full quiz, as normal; completing it switches the whole app (badges, portfolio, Telegram-link check, watch registration)
- **Cancellable** - a ✕ appears in the overlay *only* for the switch flow (first-run onboarding stays mandatory), so an accidental click doesn't trap you
- **Returning wallet** → instant restore, no quiz: profiles are saved per-wallet in `localStorage["panik_profiles_by_wallet"]`, keyed by lowercase address. Existing users are backfilled from their current flat keys on first load, so even pre-feature onboarders can switch away and back freely.

**3. Bonus fix caught during testing** - after a switch, the portfolio briefly showed the *previous* wallet's positions while the new fetch was in flight; `useWalletPositions` now resets on wallet change ([live.ts](src/panik-core/lib/live.ts)).

## Verified end-to-end (headless Edge, live API)

|---|---|
| Header chips aligned (right = onboarded wallet) | ✅ |
| Chip opens cancellable overlay (✕ present) | ✅ |
| Fresh wallet gets the quiz | ✅ |
| Cancel keeps the current wallet untouched | ✅ |
| Full switch to wallet B - header + badges + portfolio follow | ✅ |
| Switch back to A - instant, no quiz, original profile restored | ✅ |

{

  "old_string": "  // Portfolio macro metrics from the SELECTED wallet's live positions",
  "new_string": "  // Portfolio history: alert feed + score series for the selected wallet.\n  const historyWallet = boundMode\n    ? onboardedWallet\n    : selectedWallet && selectedWallet !== \"all\"\n      ? selectedWallet\n      : null;\n  const walletHistory = useWalletHistory(historyWallet);\n\n  // 30d aggregate risk series: bucket snapshots by day, protocols weighted by\n  // collateral USD (same weighting the macro Aggregate Risk Index uses).\n  const riskHistory = useMemo(() => {\n    const snaps = walletHistory?.snapshots;\n    if (!snaps || snaps.length < 2) return null;\n    const byDay = new Map<string, { weighted: number; weight: number }>();\n    for (const s of snaps) {\n      const day = s.created_at.slice(0, 10);\n      const w = Math.max(1, Number(s.collateral_usd ?? 0));\n      const cur = byDay.get(day) ?? { weighted: 0, weight: 0 };\n      cur.weighted += s.total * w;\n      cur.weight += w;\n      byDay.set(day, cur);\n    }\n    const days = [...byDay.keys()].sort();\n    if (days.length < 2) {\n      // Single day of data: fall back to the raw intra-day series.\n      return { xStart: \"today\", series: snaps.map((s) => s.total) };\n    }\n    return {\n      xStart: `${days.length}d ago`,\n      series: days.map((d) => {\n        const b = byDay.get(d)!;\n        return Math.round(b.weighted / b.weight);\n      }),\n    };\n  }, [walletHistory]);\n\n  // Portfolio macro metrics from the SELECTED wallet's live positions"
}

no on-chain transaction was sent\n              </span>\n              <button\n                onClick={onClose}\n                className=\"mt-1 w-full py-2.5 rounded-xl font-mono text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wider text-white bg-white/[0.06] hover:bg-white/[0.1] border border-white/10 cursor-pointer transition-colors\"\n              >\n                Done\n              </button>\n            </div>\n          )}\n        </motion.div>\n      </motion.div>\n    </AnimatePresence>\n  );\n}\n"
}

## Visual Risk Communication

Liquidation thresholds should be presented in an easy-to-understand manner using percentages (like 76% for Default Mode, 65% for E-Mode) to indicate different risk levels. ## Key Design Patterns

**Simplified Data Presentation**: Technical financial metrics like Collateralization, Liquidation Threshold, and Liquidation Penalty are displayed as simple percentages, eliminating the need for users to decode complicated terms.

**Color Coding**: Color coding is used effectively to highlight safety levels, giving users immediate feedback on their risk exposure.

## Progressive Disclosure

Progressive disclosure is a best practice where summary information is shown first, allowing users to drill deeper into details. Progressive disclosure widgets have a simple, clean initial view that is instantly understandable, with deeper insights available through a single click for users wanting more information.

## Real-Time Risk Monitoring

Risk dashboards offer market information such as total borrow amount, total supply, and TVL, allowing users to manage their wallet liquidation risk in one dashboard. # AI-Augmented DeFi Risk Dashboard Widgets

## Nine Proposed Widgets

**1. Risk-O-Meter**
- **Data**: Portfolio's Value at Risk (VaR) based on volatility, asset correlations, and historical data
- **At-a-Glance**: Semi-circle gauge with color progression (green to red) showing potential loss percentage
- **Pattern**: Industrial dial metaphor; enables "1-second check-in"

**2. Smart-Contract Sentinel**
- **Data**: Vulnerability scans of interacted smart contracts, severity levels of threats
- **At-a-Glance**: Severity badges (Low/High) with actual code snippet display
- **Pattern**: Code-focused alerts for transparency; color-coded severity

**3. Anomaly Stream**
- **Data**: Real-time on-chain events deviating from normal patterns (unusual swaps, governance votes)
- **At-a-Glance**: Confidence scores and event tags allow "rapid scanning"
- **Pattern**: Timeline/feed format with icon recognition and fade-in animations

**4. Oracle Health Monitor**
- **Data**: Price oracle accuracy compared against secondary data sources
- **At-a-Glance**: Node graph showing drift percentage; pulsing red lines indicate deviations
- **Pattern**: Network graph metaphor with visual alerts on problematic connections

**5. Governance Attack Predictor**
- **Data**: Malicious proposal probability, voting distribution, quorum distance
- **At-a-Glance**: Probability score paired with stacked bar chart and floating quorum marker
- **Pattern**: Combination of large probability indicator plus contextual voting breakdown

- **Data**: Simulated slippage across pools for hypothetical large trades
- **At-a-Glance**: Heatmap with color scale (green to red) identifying illiquid pools

- **Data**: Wallet history, loan health, collateral quality, governance participation
- **At-a-Glance**: Simple score bar (Poor to Excellent range)

- **Data**: Cyclical transaction routes across protocols; potential exploit paths
- **At-a-Glance**: Force-directed graph with animated red dashed lines highlighting attack vectors
- **Pattern**: Network visualization with distinct animation for critical paths

**9. Yield vs. Risk Scatter**
- **Data**: Available yield farming opportunities mapped by APY and AI risk assessment
- **At-a-Glance**: Quadrant scatter plot identifying mispriced opportunities and warning zones
- **Pattern**: Classic XY scatter plot with interactive drag-to-select and tooltip features

# DeFi Saver's Automation & Liquidation Protection Approach

Based on the documentation, DeFi Saver presents automation through these key elements:

**Trigger-Based Settings:**
The system uses ratio thresholds that users configure. For example, in leverage management, users set a "repay if below" ratio that determines when automatic adjustments execute. The documentation explains: "an auto-repay can only be executed for a user's position once their current ratio drops below their configured ('repay if below') ratio."

**Dual Verification Layers:**
DeFi Saver implements two safety mechanisms:
1. **Pre-execution checks** - transactions fail if trigger conditions aren't met
2. **On-chain outcome verification** - the transaction only completes if the user's target condition is achieved (e.g., reaching the "repay to" ratio)

**Safety Framing:**
The platform emphasizes user control by stating that automation contracts receive "rights to make adjustments on their position - but only once the user configured trigger condition is met, and fully limited by the user's configuration." This messaging highlights that adjustments are bounded by user-defined parameters.

**Monitoring Model:**
Once enabled, "Automation bots start actively monitoring" positions to execute adjustments when thresholds are reached.

The approach prioritizes predictable, conditional execution rather than discretionary intervention.

# DeFi Loan Risk UX: Problems & Solutions

## Core Problem
Current interfaces inconsistently visualize the relationship between user LTV (Loan-to-Value) and maximum LTV, making risk assessment unclear for new users.

## Identified Problems with Existing Interfaces

**Abracadabra & Sushi:**
- Use 0-100% scales where "100% = bad"
- Counterintuitive: "when my position's health is 100%, it will die"
- Progress bars increasing rightward suggest positive outcomes, but liquidation approaches
- Language (price "drops," health "falls") conflicts with visuals (health bar rises to danger)

**Aave:**
- Abstract "health factor" where 1.0 = liquidation
- No clear relationship to stated LTV percentage (e.g., 41.5%)
- Scale ending at 1 rather than zero feels arbitrary
- User research showed: familiar users tolerate it; new users find it "confusing"

**Angle:**
- Presents raw data without context, color coding, or tooltips
- Pure numbers require mental translation

## Proposed UX Improvements

**Visualization Principles:**
- Invert scales so danger decreases leftward/downward (as Alpaca demonstrates with "Kill Buffer")
- Avoid 100% to represent healthy positions
- Use 0←100 or x→0 scales instead

**Data Representation:**
- Display the buffer/margin between current LTV and liquidation threshold
- Show actionable metrics: "price at liquidation" or "required price drop until liquidation"
- Reduce overall number density

**Visual Indicators:**
- Traffic light colors (green/amber/red) for quick risk assessment
- Status labels ("Low/Medium/High" risk) eliminate abstract calculations
- Emoji or custom illustrations for severity identification
- Subtle colored dots as alternatives to full bars

## User Research Findings
Testing revealed that verbal descriptors and visual hierarchies significantly outperformed abstract ratios for non-expert users.
```

# DeFi UX Simplification Techniques

## Information Hierarchy
- Card-based layout separates distinct information chunks
- Key metrics (APY at 3.67%) displayed prominently in highlighted sections for immediate visibility
- Balance information shown alongside APY to enable quick decisions within one view

## Progressive Disclosure
- Advanced features hidden "behind easily accessible toggles"
- Two distinct modes (Default vs E-Mode) clearly separated but easily switchable
- Information icons placed strategically for optional learning at user's pace

## Data Presentation & Wording
- Technical metrics converted to simple percentages (collateralization, liquidation thresholds)
- Familiar UI patterns (dropdown menus for token selection) reduce cognitive friction
- Token symbols paired with icons and USD prices for effortless identification
- "Max" labeling clarifies full token availability

## Feedback Patterns
- Color coding highlights safety levels and risk exposure
- Risk visualization presents liquidation thresholds clearly (76% Default Mode, 65% E-Mode)
- Consistent risk parameter presentation across modes enables comparison

## Design Defaults
- The case study emphasizes "Default Mode" as the primary user pathway, implying simplified settings as the starting point for newcomers

## Mobile Optimization
- Touch-friendly design and scrollable layout preserve information density without screen clutter

Research done and written up as [UX_RESEARCH_DEFI_DASHBOARDS.md](docs/technical-docs/UX_RESEARCH_DEFI_DASHBOARDS.md) for the team. The short version:

## The 7 patterns that make DeFi data understandable

1. **Verbal beats numeric, dollars beat percentages** - user testing shows non-experts parse "High risk" and "price at liquidation" far faster than abstract ratios. Aave's bare health factor is the canonical *bad* example. *(PANIK mostly does this already - the gap is the Watch tab's big HF number standing alone.)*
2. **Scale direction must match the story** - "health 100% = death" bars that fill toward danger confuse everyone. *(We're safe: our number is explicitly RISK, rises = worse.)*
3. **Buffer is the hero metric** - the margin to liquidation (Alpaca's "Kill Buffer") is the most decision-useful number, yet almost nobody headlines it. *(We show it, but buried as dimension 4.)*
4. **One-second check-in** - a single gauge readable at a glance, details behind a click (Risk-O-Meter pattern; Zerion's summary-first hierarchy).
5. **Time series anchor the page** - every top tracker (Zerion/DeBank/Zapper) leads with a value-over-time chart + activity feed. *(We shipped exactly this pair today.)*
6. **Yield-vs-Risk scatter** - plotting opportunities as APY × risk with a "danger zone" quadrant is the strongest discovery visual, and **no mainstream tracker can build it because none has a calibrated risk score - we do**. This is PANIK's signature-feature opportunity.
7. **Automation must feel bounded** - DeFi Saver wins trust by saying what the bot *cannot* do ("only at your trigger, fully limited by your configuration"). Ready-made copy pattern for when the auto-repay card returns.

## Prioritized backlog (in the doc)

| Priority | Item | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plain-language tooltips on every metric | S |
| 2 | Buffer-to-liquidation as headline stat; HF always paired with its translation | S |
| 3 | Collateral-value trend beside the risk chart (data already in `/api/history`) | S |
| 4 | Semi-circle aggregate risk gauge + one-line verdict | M |
| 5 | **Yield-vs-Risk scatter in Compass** (signature feature) | M |
| 6 | Bounded-automation copy for the future auto-repay | S |

Notable validation: today's QA work (dollar verdicts, scenario chips, band colors, history chart + feed) is squarely aligned with what the research says works - the backlog above is refinement, not rework.

{
  "file_path": "c:\\Users\\ASUS\\Documents\\Github Projects\\panik_waitlist\\src\\panik-core\\components\\InfoTip.tsx",
  "content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport React, { useRef, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { createPortal } from \"react-dom\";\nimport { HelpCircle } from \"lucide-react\";\n\n/**\n * Plain-language metric tooltip (UX research backlog #1: every metric gets a\n * one-sentence explanation). Rendered through a portal with fixed positioning\n * so it never gets clipped by the cards' overflow-hidden containers, and\n * flips below the anchor near the top of the viewport. Keyboard-accessible\n * (focusable, shows on focus).\n */\nexport function InfoTip(props: { text: string; className?: string }) {\n  const anchor = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);\n  const [pos, setPos] = useState<{ x: number; y: number; below: boolean } | null>(null);\n\n  const show = () => {\n    const r = anchor.current?.getBoundingClientRect();\n    if (!r) return;\n    const below = r.top < 96; // not enough headroom: render under the icon\n    setPos({ x: r.left + r.width / 2, y: below ? r.bottom : r.top, below });\n  };\n  const hide = () => setPos(null);\n\n  return (\n    <span\n      ref={anchor}\n      tabIndex={0}\n      aria-label={props.text}\n      className={`inline-flex align-middle outline-none ${props.className ?? \"\"}`}\n      onMouseEnter={show}\n      onMouseLeave={hide}\n      onFocus={show}\n      onBlur={hide}\n    >\n      <HelpCircle className=\"w-3 h-3 text-white/25 hover:text-panik-orange transition-colors cursor-help shrink-0\" />\n      {pos &&\n        createPortal(\n          <span\n            role=\"tooltip\"\n            className={`fixed z-[300] w-60 -translate-x-1/2 pointer-events-none ${pos.below ? \"\" : \"-translate-y-full\"}`}\n            style={{ left: pos.x, top: pos.below ? pos.y + 6 : pos.y - 6 }}\n          >\n            <span className=\"block p-2.5 rounded-lg bg-[#1A1D26] border border-white/10 text-[10px] font-sans normal-case tracking-normal font-normal text-white/85 leading-relaxed shadow-2xl text-left\">\n              {props.text}\n            </span>\n          </span>,\n          document.body,\n        )}\n    </span>\n  );\n}\n"
}
```

## What shipped

**New [InfoTip](src/panik-core/components/InfoTip.tsx) component** - dependency-free, portal-rendered (never clipped by card containers), flips below the icon near the viewport top, keyboard-accessible (focusable, `aria-label`, `role="tooltip"`).

**18 tooltips, every one a plain-language sentence** following the research rule (verbal + consequence, not jargon):

| Surface | Metrics covered |
|---|---|
| **Watch** | Panik Risk Index (what the 0-100 means + where alerts fire), Health Factor ("below 1.00 the protocol can liquidate you - the buffer matters more than the raw number"), Position LTV, and all four Top Risk Drivers with their weights |
| **Risk breakdown panel** | Panik Risk Score (with the band thresholds), all four weighted components, LTV, HF, Liquidation Price, **Buffer** ("your real safety margin - the most decision-useful number here"), Pool Utilization, Supply APY, Pool TVL |
| **Portfolio** | Monitored Capital, Monitored Liabilities (defines Net LTV inline), Aggregate Risk Index (explains the collateral weighting) |

Note the deliberate copy choices from the research: the HF tooltip actively redirects users toward the buffer (pattern #3), and weight percentages appear in the driver tooltips so the composite math is learnable in place.

Verified: tsc clean (only the pre-existing `panik-founding` errors), tooltips confirmed on all three tabs in headless Edge including the overflow-container case. Live on **localhost:3001** now.

Next up from the backlog when you're ready: **#2 buffer-as-headline** (small) or **#5 the Yield-vs-Risk scatter** (the differentiator). And the working tree now holds QA round 2 + the UX research doc + these tooltips - say the word to commit and push.

### 🤖 Claude *(2026-07-03 14:31:34)*

Clean (only the known `panik-founding` errors). Here's the journey, before and after:

## Before (the unfriendly version)

```
Portfolio ──── dead end, no hint where positions live
  └─ user must GUESS that "Compass" = open positions
       └─ card → Open Position → modal (confusing "Deposit (wstETH)" + USD amounts)

Watch simulator ── convinced by the numbers? Tough - navigate back to
                   Compass and find the card again.
```

## After

```
① Portfolio ─[+ Open Position]─> Compass ─[Open Position]─> modal ─[confirm]  = 3 clicks
② Fresh wallet: "No positions yet" banner ─[Explore Compass →]─> same path
③ Watch simulator ─[Open This Position]─> modal ─[confirm]                    = 2 clicks
④ Breakdown panel ─[Open Position]─> modal                                    (existing)
```

## What changed

1. **Portfolio header** now carries a primary **`+ Open Position`** button - the action is visible from the landing tab, no guessing.
2. **Empty-wallet path**: a fresh wallet gets a *"No positions yet - browse risk-scored opportunities matched to your moderate profile"* banner with **Explore Compass →**. New users are never at a dead end.
3. **Simulate-to-open**: the Watch simulator header has **Open This Position** - the simulator is where conviction forms, so the action now lives at the moment of decision instead of two navigations away. This is the flow no competitor has: *stress-test first, open second*.
4. **Modal unit fix**: `Deposit (wstETH)` with dollar amounts was a genuine comprehension bug - now reads **"Deposit amount (USD, supplied as wstETH)"**, and the receipt says "$5,000 *of* wstETH supplied".
5. **Compass subtitle** now says "Find **and open** positions matched to your risk profile" - the tab announces its job.

Every entry point converges on the same demo modal, so there's one flow to maintain. Verified 5/5 in headless Edge (both journeys click-through end to end), tsc clean, live on **localhost:3001**.

One deliberate omission: I did *not* put "Open Position" on the **Outside Your Profile** cards - forcing users through "Force Audit" for positions beyond their risk profile is honest friction that matches PANIK's whole premise. Flag if BD disagrees.

The tree now holds QA round 2 + UX research doc + tooltips + this journey work - ready to commit and push on your word.
